body.statement: Using the second-order staircase alignment handle, derive a primitive block-ratio expression \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), common across \(n\), such that \[c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\le\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\] for every vanishing tail sequence \(\eta_n\), where \(\Delta_n^*\) is optimized over the explicitly defined slice \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\). Establish the coverage frontier in this finite-slice experiment: \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) must imply \(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0\); conversely, for every primitive candidate \(\beta\) with \(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^{\dagger}\) and \(\beta_n(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) along a subsequence on which \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) is bounded away from zero, construct one complete staggered low-rank triangular array \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) satisfying \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\ge c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\), and \(\liminf_n\Gamma_n(P_n)>0\). The derivation must first test whether the balanced strong-factor rank-one second-order remainder is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\); if so, \(\Delta^{\dagger}\) must use the smaller attained scale.
body.justification: The honest open content is necessity: published norm bounds can be sufficient yet unattainable by any legal low-rank staircase panel.
body.gap: Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Koike give nearly sharp generic vector-sum arrays, but those arrays need not arise from the Choi--Yuan debiasing map; no source establishes an attainable panel-specific converse.
body.consumer: A resolved frontier tells empirical researchers exactly how far the event horizon may grow without ad hoc band inflation and prevents overclaiming a coarse perturbation bound as sharp.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact second-order Choi--Yuan remainder on a legal balanced rank-one triangular array and a matching lower bound for its \(1-\eta_n\) quantile with signs aligned across horizons.
obligation.obstruction: The published envelope \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) is only an upper perturbation expression.  The frozen definition of \(\widehat M^0\) names the estimator but omits its objective, tuning parameters, KKT equations, and debiasing formula, so the mandated early-kill second-order calculation is not determined by the available primitives.  The two-horizon witness certifies linear covariance only and supplies no nonlinear-remainder lower bound.
obligation.attempted: First tested whether the rank-one witness could yield an attained remainder from the displayed influence coefficients.  Those coefficients determine only the first-order term; every second-order term depends on the unspecified estimator map.  Also compared the exact modulus definition with \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\): a simultaneous block tail bound would prove only the upper inequality, while successive norm inequalities provide no reverse inequality or undercoverage sign.
obligation.partial_result:
The definitions do identify the exact, but nonprimitive, frontier:
\[
\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
=\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
\inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}.
\]
If a simultaneous block event of the form isolated in the uniform
influence partial result were available with tail probability at most
\(\eta_n\), it would imply the computable one-sided bound
\[
\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
This is only an upper bound.  Each term in
\(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) results from norm inequalities, and neither an
upper perturbation bound nor the linear two-horizon covariance witness
implies that any legal low-rank panel attains one of those terms with an
aligned sign.  The frozen construction of \(\widehat M^0\) names the
Choi--Yuan procedure but does not give its objective, tuning parameters,
KKT equations, or debiasing formula.  Therefore its exact second-order
remainder cannot be computed from the frozen primitives, and no lower
bound comparable to a primitive block-ratio expression has been proved.
